Made by... D.S.I. Logan    Forwarded by C. [Signature]

On the morning of May 22, 1939, Sergeant-Major
S. Sakamoto of the Japanese River Police, Floating
Restaurant, The Bund, called at Headquarters with
information that a certain book binding works in
Sincza District was binding books of an anti-Japanese
and communistic nature and solicited assistance to
search the concern in question.

Assistance was rendered by D.S. Anderson, D.S.
Komoshita, D.S.I. Lino Chung Chien and J.D.S. 141
Tang Hung Sung of Special Branch, D.F.S. Yokoyama of
Special Political Office, D.S. Sorrie (Sinzə).
The party was led by Sergeant-Major S. Sakamoto to
the Tsing Yih Book Binding Works (青益印書裝訂所),
House 56, Lane 741, off Chengtu Road, where a large
quantity of books of anti-Japanese and communist nature
comprising the following seven kinds were seized:-

1. Inside Red China (續西行漫記) (Chinese edition)
by Nym Wales.
2. Activities and Works of the Anti-Japanese University,
(Yenan).
3. Essays of Li Da Chao (守常全集) (a late prominent
communist arrested and executed in Peiping in 1928.)
4. General Principles of the Communist International.
5. Socialist Thought (containing essays of a national
salvation and anti-aggression nature).
6. A text book on the history of Communist Party of
U.S.S.R..
7. Life in the Western Front (containing articles bear-
ing on the life of members of the North Western
War Area Service Group).

（批：Raiding van made two trips - half full in each trip.）

1939年5月22日上午，日本水上警察警部长 S. Sakamoto 来到外滩浮码头餐厅总部，提供情报称新闸区某装订所正在装订反日及共产主义性质的书籍，并请求协助搜查该商号。

特务科的安德森（Anderson）巡佐、Komoshita 巡佐、林忠坚（Lino Chung Chien）副督察长和第141号华籍侦探唐洪松（Tang Hung Sung），特务政治办公室的横山（Yokoyama）副巡佐，以及新闸捕房的 Sorrie 巡佐提供了协助。一行人由警部长 S. Sakamoto 带领，前往位于成都路741弄56号的青益印书装订所，在那里查获了大量反日及共产主义性质的书籍，共包括以下七种：

1. 尼姆·威尔斯（Nym Wales）著《续西行漫记》（中文版）
2. 抗日大学（延安）的活动与著作
3. 《守常全集》（李大钊文集）（李大钊为前著名共产党员，1928年在北平被捕并处决。）
4. 共产国际一般原则
5. 《社会主义思想》（包含救国及反侵略性质的文章）
6. 苏联共产党历史教科书
7. 《西线生活》（包含有关西北战区服务团成员生活的文章）

（批注：搜查车往返两次——每次半满。）

My name is Wu Yu San (吳玉山), aged 48, a native
of Yangchow, married, employed as accountant and reside
in the Tsing Yih Book Binding Works, Lane 741, No. 56,
Chengtu Road.

At the age of 10, I began to study in a primary
school in Yangchow. Five years later I joined a
candy shop in my native place as an apprentice. I
remained in that trade as shop assistant until November
1936, when I came to Shanghai in the hope of obtaining
a more advantageous employment.

Through the recommendation of a friend of mine
named Tsang Yu Foong (張裕豐), who is also a native
of Yangchow, and at present lives in that city, I became
a book-binder in the Tsing Yih Book Binding Works, 56/741
Chengtu Road, immediately after my arrival in Shanghai.

Following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hosti-
lities in Shanghai in August, 1937, the accountant of
the Tsing Yih Book-binding Works, returned to Yangchow and
I was appointed by the proprietor, Wong Soong Yuin (王松雲)
to fill the vacancy.

Regarding the books seized by the Municipal Police
in the binding works I do not know who had ordered the
binding. All transactions between the book-binding works
and its customers were conducted by the proprietor, Wong
Soong Yuin, and the Broker, Wong Moo Tse (王慕之) who
is a nephew of the former. Both Wong Soong Yuin and
Wong Moo Tse live in the Tsing Yih Book-binding Works.

My name is Woo Hsuen Zu, aged 24, a native of
Sungyu ( 上虞 ), Chekiang, single, student, residing at No.174
Rue Ratard.

At the age of 7 I began to study in my native home.
Ten years later, I completed the primary and junior middle
school courses and came to Shanghai joining the Senior Middle
School of the Utopia University, South Station Road, Nantao.

In July, 1937, I returned to my native home as the
school began its summer vacation. My father died when I was
8 years old; my mother is alive and is at present living in
Sungyu. I have three elder brothers; the eldest, Woo Zoong
Sz ( 胡仲持 ), residing at 174 Rue Ratard, is a sub-editor of
the Shun Pao, he having been in that employment for the past
ten years. My other two brothers, Woo Sz Liu ( 胡師柳 ), and
Woo Hsueh Yuen ( 胡學愿 ), are at present in Shaoshing and
Ningpo respectively. Woo Sz Liu is a departmental chief of
the Shaoshing Hsien Government while Woo Hsueh Yuan is a
manager of a native bank in Ningpo.

In August, 1937, the Sino-Japanese hostilities broke
out in Shanghai and the Utopia University temporarily suspended
functioning. Owing to sickness I did not come back to
Shanghai until December, 1938.

The Utopia University at present operates classes
on the premises of Kwang Hsia Middle School, 40 Moulmein Road,
and I intend to re-join the school when the next Autumn
simister begins. I studied chemistry in the University and
it will take me two years more to complete the course.

本人名叫胡學恕，现年24岁，浙江上虞人，未婚，学生，现住拉达路（Rue Ratard）174号。

本人7岁时开始在家乡读书。十年后，修完小学及初中课程，来到上海，进入位于南市南站路的私立大同大学附属高中就读。

1937年7月，因学校放暑假，我返回家乡。本人8岁时父亲去世；母亲健在，目前居住在上虞。我有三个哥哥；长兄胡仲持（Woo Zoong Sz），住拉达路174号，系《申报》副编辑，已在此任职十年。另外两个哥哥，胡師柳（Woo Sz Liu）和胡學愿（Woo Hsueh Yuen），目前分别在绍兴和宁波。胡師柳任绍兴县政府科长，胡學愿任宁波一家钱庄的经理。

1937年8月，中日战事在上海爆发，大同大学暂时停课。因病直到1938年12月我才回到上海。

目前大同大学在莫尔美路（Moulmein Road）40号光华中学内上课，我打算在下个秋季学期开始时复学。我在大学攻读化学，还需两年才能完成学业。

I have no connections with the Foh Zoe, the publisher
of the book entitled "Inside Red China". As far as I know,
Foh Zoe has its main office in Hongkong, and the office
established in my brother's home at 174 Rue Ratard is its
Shanghai Branch. The director of this publication office
in Hongkong is one Wong Chi Yuan (王季源) a friend of
my brother, who was the editor of the Shun Pao Weekly prior
to August, 1937. The Shanghai Branch of this publication
office is in charge of one Chu Tseng Lai (朱青瀾). He
leased the downstairs room from my brother at a rent of $55.00
per mensem about 6 or 7 months ago.

In the evening of May 22, 1939, Chu learned that the
Police had seized a large number of copies of the book entitled
"Inside Red China" from a book-binding works, through reading
the evening news of that day and he immediately removed his
property, leaving behind only some furniture. I don't know
his present whereabouts nor his past activities. He is
about 45 years old, wears a long gown, uses spectacles and
has the appearance of a business man.

Chen Kwan Jui (陳冠球), who was taken into custody
by the Police together with me in my home, is a former school-
mate of mine. He is at present unemployed and came to live
in my brother's home in March 1939. I knew that he was
previously arrested by the French Police in connection with
the national salvation movement and was later sentenced to a
certain term of imprisonment.

I have never joined any political party or taken
part in local national salvation movements.

Wogan

French Concession
Shanghai.
Police Headquarters
Political Branch

No. 4391/R

May 23, 1939.

REPORT.
Subject: Search effected at No.174 Rue Ratard,
Alleged Stock of Anti-Japanese books.
Ref: Assistance to the Settlement Police
Sino-Japanese Hostilities.

At 8.30 p.m. on May 23, 1939, Sub-Inspector LOGAN
and Detective Sergeant Andersen (Special Branch) of the
Settlement Police came and requested our assistance
with a view to effecting a raid at No.174 Rue Ratard
where a stock of books of an anti-Japanese nature
entitled "Voyage in the West" (续西游记) was to be
found.

This raid was carried out in consequence of
information received by the Settlement Police from
the Japanese Authorities who alleged that a stock
of these books was to be found at the "Tsing Yih"
(清益) Printing office, Chengtu Road.

A raid carried out at this address by the
Settlement Police resulted on May 22, 1939 in the
discovery of numerous copies of this book and the
proprietor of this printing office pointed out that
a complete stock was to be found in the French
Concession at No.174 Rue Ratard.

The assistance as requested was rendered
and we accompanied the members of Settlement Police
to the above address. On arrival the chief tenant,
Hu Zong Shih (胡仲持) of the address told us that
it was true that a stock of books had been deposited
in a room on the ground floor of the house, but that
on May 22, 1939, one Tsu Tseng Lai (朱曾濑) responsible for these books, had transferred them to
an unknown address.

1939年5月23日晚8时30分，租界警务处的副督察洛根（LOGAN）和侦探警佐安德森（Andersen）（特别分部）前来请求我方协助，旨在突击搜查拉塔德路174号，据称该处藏有一批名为《续西游记》的反日性质书籍。

此次突击行动是基于租界警务处从日本当局获得的情报而采取的，日方声称在成都路“清益”印刷所藏有一批此类书籍。

租界警务处于1939年5月22日对该地址进行了突击搜查，结果发现了大量该书的副本，该印刷所的业主指出，完整的库存可在法租界拉塔德路174号找到。

应请求提供了协助，我们陪同租界警务处人员前往上述地址。到达后，该地址的主要承租人胡仲持（Hu Zong Shih）告诉我们，确实有一批书籍存放在该房屋底楼的一个房间内，但负责这些书籍的朱曾濑（Tsu Tseng Lai，音译）已于1939年5月22日将其转移至一个未知的地址。

TRANSLATION.

Summarised review of a book entitled
"Voyage in the West" (西行漫记)(Inside Red China)
------------------

This book written by Mr. Nym Wales, was published
in 1939 by the "Fu Zoh" ( no address) Society. It contains
567 pages.

In the chapters I to IV (pages I to 519) the
organisation of the Chinese Communist Party in the regions
occupied by Red troops is discussed.

In the chapter V (pages 513 to 565) the Sino-
Japanese conflict is discussed. The author outlines in
particular the tactics of the Red troops in the military
operations directed against the Japanese in North China.
In conclusion the author criticises Japan's aggressive
policy in China, a policy which will entail Japan's decline.

In the Supplement (pages 569 to 592) there is
given the biography of 86 Chinese Communist leaders.
pages.zh:
译文。

题为《西行漫记》（Inside Red China）一书的摘要评论
------------------

本书由尼姆·威尔斯（Nym Wales）先生撰写，于1939年由“复社”（Fu Zoh，无地址）出版。全书共567页。

在第一至第四章（第1至519页）中，讨论了红军占领地区中国共产党的组织情况。

在第五章（第513至565页）中，讨论了中日冲突。作者特别概述了红军在华北针对日本的军事行动中的战术。最后，作者批评了日本在中国的侵略政策，认为该政策将导致日本的衰落。

在附录（第569至592页）中，列出了86位中国共产党领导人的传记。

SUPPLEMENTARY REPORT.
----------------------

Search carried out by the Japanese with the
assistance of the Settlement Police in the "Pou Yi"
____________________Printing Office.____________________

The "Pou Yi" printing office, whose headquarters are
situated at No.56 "Li Yun Fang" alleyway, North Chengtu
Road, is run by one named WANG SUNG YUN, native of Shanghai.
It prints principally books and hand-bills.
Quite recently this printing office undertook the
publication of a book entitled "Red Star Over China",
written by Mr. Edgar SNOW, an American journalist.
Yesterday at about noon Japanese civilians with
the assistance of detectives and members of the Central
Police Station of the Settlement raided it. In the course
of the search 1,500 copies approximately of the above
mentioned book and copies of other revues were seized.
Mr. WU SHAO LING, accountant of the printing office was
taken to the Station for interrogation.

References: Sin Wan Pao and other newspapers
of May 23, 1939.

补充报告。
----------------------

在日本人协助下，由租界警务处在“博益”印刷所进行的搜查。

“博益”印刷所总部设在成都北路李云坊56号，由一名名为王松云（WANG SUNG YUN，音译）的上海人经营。
主要印刷书籍和传单。
最近，该印刷所承印了美国记者埃德加·斯诺（Edgar SNOW）先生撰写的《红星照耀中国》一书。
昨天中午左右，日本平民在租界中央捕房的侦探和警员的协助下对该印刷所进行了突击搜查。在搜查过程中，查获了约1,500册上述书籍及其他期刊的副本。
该印刷所的会计吴绍林（WU SHAO LING，音译）先生被带往捕房接受讯问。

参考：1939年5月23日的《新闻报》及其他报纸。

STATEMENT of one HU YUEH SU (胡月蘇)

My name is HU YUEH SU, 24 years of age, native of
Siaoshing, student of Utopia University, Moulmein Road,
residing at No. 174 Rue Ratard with my brother HU ZONG SHIH.
WANG CHI YUEN, proprietor of the books deposited
in the room on the ground floor, is at present in Hongkong.
One named TSU TSENG IAI is responsible for the books; the
latter moved yesterday afternoon taking them away with
him after having read from the newspapers about the
discovery of a stock of books in the "Tsing Yi" printing
office, Chengtu Road.
I heard that these books were printed by the
Chinese Science Corporation, Avenue Foch.
I believe they were removed into the American Sector
where Tsu Tseng Iai thinks himself in greater security.

译文。
----------

胡月苏（HU YUEH SU）的供词

我叫胡月苏，24岁，绍兴人，慕尔鸣路乌托邦大学学生，与我的哥哥胡仲持居住在拉塔德路174号。
存放在底楼房间的书籍所有者王季原目前在香港。
一名名为朱曾赖（TSU TSENG IAI，音译）的人负责这些书籍；后者在报纸上看到成都路“清益”印刷所发现一批书籍的报道后，于昨天下午带着书籍搬走。
我听说这些书籍是由霞飞路的中国科学公司印刷的。
我相信它们已被转移至美租界防区，朱曾赖认为那里更安全。

TRANSLATION.

Statement of one named CHEN KWEI CHIEU (陈贵球)

My name is CHEN KWEI CHIEU(I) (陈贵球) 28 years
of age, native of Haimen, student in the finishing course
of the "Chi Ying" University (健行), 406 Foochow Road
(1st floor), residing at No.174 Rue Ratard.

It is my mother, who is at present in a village
called "Ching Hai Tseng" Haimen, who provides for me.

The rooms on the ground floor are rented by one
WANG CHI YUEN, who according to the chief tenant, named
Hu YUEH SU, is at present in Hongkong.

I saw a large number of books deposited in the
centre room of the ground floor.

A man named TSU TSENG LAI (朱曾濂), in charge
of the sale of deposited books, suddenly removed on May 22
in the afternoon to an unknown destination, taking away
all these books.

Since my conditional release I joined the
Kuomintang and I ceased all political activities.

At the request of my mother I continue to study.

I do not associate with TSU TSENG LAI and I
am ignorant of his activities.

-------------------------

(I) He was sentenced to three years' impt. on February 27,
1937 by the 3rd Section of the High Court, for
communist activities.
pages.zh:
译文。

名为陈贵球（CHEN KWEI CHIEU）的供词

我叫陈贵球(I)（陈贵球），28岁，海门人，福州路406号（二楼）“健行”大学结业班学生，居住在拉塔德路174号。

目前由我在海门一个叫“青海增”（Ching Hai Tseng，音译）的村庄的母亲供养。

底楼的房间由王季原租用，据主要承租人胡学苏（Hu YUEH SU）称，他目前在香港。

我看到大量书籍存放在底楼的中间房间。

一名名为朱曾濂（TSU TSENG LAI，音译）的男子，负责销售寄存的书籍，于5月22日下午突然搬离，去向不明，带走了所有这些书籍。

自获准缓刑释放以来，我加入了国民党，并停止了所有政治活动。

应母亲的要求，我继续学业。

我不与朱曾濂来往，也不了解他的活动。

-------------------------

(I) 他因共产主义活动，于1937年2月27日被高等法院第三庭判处三年监禁。

TRANSLATION.

Statement of one HU ZONG SHIH (胡仲持)
--------------------------------------

My name is HU ZONG SHIH, 40 years of age, native
of Shaoshing, editor of the "Shun Pao" newspaper; former
interpreter in the "Hava" News agency, residing at No.174
Rue Retard.

The ground floor rooms have been rented since
a year to one WANG CHI YUEI, who is now in Hongkong.
A man named TSU TSENG LAI is in charge of the stock of
books which were deposited at this address.

I read in the local press that a stock of
books has been discovered in a printing office in
Chengtu Road. It was following the reading of that
article that TSU TSENG LAI removed on May 22 in the
afternoon, taking away the books with him.

HU YUEH SU is my brother and CHEN KEI CHIM
a friend of my brother, reside in the upper room of
my house.

It was Tsu Tseng Lai who gave me the book entitled
"Voyage in the West" which you seized in my room.

Prior to leaving Tsu Tseng Lai told us that
the books would be deposited in the American Defence
Sector where he thinks he will be safe.
pages.zh:
译文。

胡仲持（HU ZONG SHIH）的供词
--------------------------------------

我叫胡仲持，40岁，绍兴人，《申报》编辑；前“哈瓦斯”通讯社翻译，居住在拉塔德路174号。

底楼房间一年前已租给王季悦（WANG CHI YUEI，音译），他现在香港。
一名名为朱曾赖（TSU TSENG LAI，音译）的男子负责存放在此地址的书籍库存。

我从本地报刊上读到，在成都路的一家印刷所发现了一批书籍。正是在读了那篇文章后，朱曾赖于5月22日下午搬走，并带走了书籍。

胡学苏是我的兄弟，陈贵钦（CHEN KEI CHIM，音译）是我兄弟的朋友，住在我家楼上的房间里。

是你们在我房间里查获的那本名为《西行漫记》的书，是朱曾赖给我的。

离开前，朱曾赖告诉我们，书籍将被存放在美军防区，他认为那里很安全。

MAY 23 1939

Books Seized at Request
Of Japanese Authorities

At the request of the Japanese
authorities, detectives attached to the
Special Branch of the Shanghai
Municipal Police raided a Chinese
book-binding establishment at House
56, Lane 741 North Chengtu Road,
shortly after noon yesterday and
confiscated a large number of books
found on the premises.
The books, it was understood, were
handed over to the detectives without
any difficulty and were transported
to headquarters in a police van.
No details were available by a
late hour last night regarding the
number of volumes thus seized, their
contents or their owners.

In the afternoon of June 27, 1939, Mr. Hashizumi,
Chancellor attached to the Japanese Consular Police,
called at Headquarters and requested assistance to
seize some 67 different kinds of books and magazines
from bookstores in the Settlement. D.S.I. Logan,
D.S. Lockwood, D.S. Mizoguchi and D.S.I. Liao together
with Mr. Hashizumi and a party under him visited the
Wu Chow Bookstore, 221 Shantung Road, and the Kwang
Ming Bookstore, 296 Foochow Road. A total of
6,818 copies of books and magazines of a national
salvation, pro-communist and anti-Japanese nature were
seized at the Wu Chow Bookstore and 166 copies at the
Kwang Ming Bookstore, all of which were removed to
Police Headquarters. Lists of the books and magazines
seized at the two bookstores aforesaid are attached
hereto as appendices "A" and "B".

with Mr. Hashizumi and a party of Japanese Consular

the International Settlement. D.S. Lockwood,

and the Van Yih (万叶) Bookstore, 11 Yen Ning Li,

magazines and 3,600 sheets of national salvation
songs, all of which were removed to Police Headquarters.
